name: col_substr
title: Substring(s) of an ANSI colored string

origin.description: substr() that counts visible characters and keeps the surrounding ANSI codes.

arguments.name: start
arguments.text: First visible character, recycled to x.

arguments.name: stop
arguments.text: Last visible character, recycled to x.

origin.details: Positions follow the string with styles removed. Codes that open before the slice, and codes that close after it, are copied onto the result so the slice keeps its color. A start past the end is empty. Zero and negative starts are treated as 1 by substr. NA in start or stop is an error. An empty x is returned unchanged.
origin.value: A character vector the same length as x.
origin.example:
str <- paste(red("red"), "default", green("green"))
cat(col_substr(str, 1, 5), "\n", sep="")
cat(col_substr(str, 3, 7), "\n", sep="")

translation.description: substr() that counts visible characters and keeps the surrounding ANSI codes.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string or a list of strings.

translation.details: Visible positions ignore CSI sequences. A start or stop that is not an integer is an error. A string is one element, so col_substr("red", 1, 2) is the first two characters, not a substring of a list.
translation.value: The sliced string, or a list when x has more than one element.
translation.example:
text = red("red") + " default " + green("green")
print(col_substr(text, 1, 5))
print(col_substr(text, 3, 7))
